options.text: The protection and preservation of natural resources and biodiversity
The process of classifying organisms
The destruction of habitats for human use
The study of how organisms evolve

questions.explanation: Conservation is the protection and preservation of natural resources and biodiversity. It aims to maintain healthy ecosystems, protect endangered species, and ensure that resources are available for future generations.

options.text: The genetic code of a single species
The variety of living organisms in an area
The total number of organisms in the world
The number of ecosystems on Earth

questions.explanation: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living organisms in an area. It includes genetic diversity (variation within species), species diversity (number of different species), and ecosystem diversity (variety of habitats).

options.text: Stopping all use of natural resources
Building more factories and cities
Using all resources as quickly as possible
Meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs

questions.explanation: Sustainable development means meeting the needs of the present generation without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. It involves balancing economic growth with environmental protection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an ex-situ conservation method?

options.text: Creating a nature reserve
Breeding endangered species in zoos and seed banks
Protecting a coral reef
Banning hunting in a forest

questions.explanation: Ex-situ conservation means conserving species outside their natural habitat. Examples include breeding programmes in zoos, seed banks, and botanical gardens. In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, such as nature reserves.

questions.stem: Why is maintaining biodiversity important for ecosystems?

options.text: Because only one species is needed for an ecosystem to function
Because biodiversity has no effect on ecosystem function
Because greater biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable and resilient
Because all species perform the same role in an ecosystem

questions.explanation: Greater biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable and resilient to changes. With more species, ecosystems are better able to recover from disturbances, and the loss of one species has less impact because other species can fulfil similar roles.

options.text: Services provided by conservation organisations
The number of species in an ecosystem
Benefits that humans receive from functioning ecosystems, such as clean air and water
The cost of maintaining national parks

questions.explanation: Ecosystem services are the benefits that humans receive from functioning ecosystems. These include clean air and water, pollination of crops, flood control, carbon storage, and provision of food and medicines.

questions.stem: Fish quotas are an example of conservation because they:

options.text: Increase the price of fish for consumers
Ban all fishing permanently
Allow unlimited fishing of any species
Limit the number of fish caught to allow populations to recover

questions.explanation: Fish quotas limit the number or weight of fish that can be caught, allowing fish populations to maintain sustainable numbers. This prevents overfishing and helps ensure that fish stocks can recover and remain available long-term.
